question.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(-9,6)$ lies on the curve $y=f(\frac{1}{3}x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=f(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)=f(3\cdot (\frac{1}{3}x)),$ the function $y=f(x)$ represents a compression of the function $y=f(\frac{1}{3}x)$ by a factor of $3$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of dividing the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(\frac{1}{3}x)$ by $3.$

Therefore, the point $(-9,6)$ on $f(\frac{1}{3}x)$ is mapped to the point $(\frac{(-9)}{3},6)=(-3,6),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y=f(x).$
